blocks.heading: Proof an Accounts Manager Can Check
rows: A bank reconciliation you completed on practice data
Explain the differences you found and how you cleared them.
It is a daily task and reveals attention to detail.
A GST return prepared for a practice or small client
Say which sections you filled and how you checked input credit.
Many small firms need someone who can do this.
A month-end checklist you wrote
Show the steps and what you would check first.
Process thinking is rare in freshers.
Excel work: lookups, pivots, a clean MIS sheet
Offer to share the sheet or explain one formula.
Spreadsheet skill speeds up almost every accounting job.
A short certificate or course with a project attached
Name the project, not just the certificate.
Employers trust output more than a pass mark.

blocks.heading: Weak Lines in an Accounting Interview
rows: I was weak in other subjects.
It sounds like accounting is a fallback and invites a quick rejection.
Say what in accounting made sense to you and give one example.
I just want a stable job.
It gives the employer nothing to evaluate.
Talk about the work you can do now and what you want to learn.
I know Tally.
Too vague and easy to test.
Say which version, what tasks and what you produced.
I want to become a CFO.
Sounds unrealistic for an entry role.
Say you want to grow step by step and name the next role.

blocks.heading: Growth and AI Behind an Accounting Answer
rows: Data and business analysis
Higher ceiling when paired with SQL and dashboards.
Needs more technical learning.
Banking operations
Larger employers and structured training.
Targets and shift work vary.

blocks.heading: Practice Rounds Before the Interview
rows: Round 1: your story
Write one accuracy example.
A stranger can repeat your story back accurately after one hearing. Field check: task, result and check method are clear.
Round 2: delivery
Practise the answer aloud and time it.
You finish in about a minute and it sounds like you, not a script. Field check: under a minute.
Round 3: the hard question
Prepare a reconciliation walkthrough.
Your answer to the question you fear holds up without notes. Field check: you can explain it in simple words.
Round 4: full mock
Run a mock with the five follow-ups.
You keep the same facts when a follow-up changes the angle. Field check: steady answers on software and growth.
